versions.changelog:
## Features
- Frames are no longer taken from inside media segments, so intros, credits, recaps, previews, and commercials stay out of generated artwork
- New Avoid Media Segments setting under Frame Extraction, with a checkbox for each kind of segment to avoid, all on by default
- Segments come from a media segment provider turned on for the library, so items without any extract as before

## Developer
- Changing which segments are avoided discards the idle frame pools, so the next refresh extracts under the new choice

## Features
- New Cleanup Backdrops scheduled task under Library that reduces every item on the server to a single backdrop, keeping the first and deleting the rest along with their files
- The task has no default schedule, so it only runs when started by hand or on a trigger you add

## Features
- Primary and thumb images can name a second and third design, adding their versions of the same frames to the Edit Images picker
- New Edit Images Cache setting for how long rendered choices stay available, default 30 minutes
- Edit Images reuses the choices it already rendered when switching image type or page, instead of rendering every image again

## Fixes
- The Edit Images cache is bounded by size at 256 MB and releases expired images on its own, instead of holding them until the next render
- Every design in one Edit Images render draws from the same frames, even while other items are extracting
- Posters pass over a logo Jellyfin only knows by web address and use the next logo that can be read

## Developer
- Settings saved before 12.0.2.0 are no longer brought forward, so update through 12.0.2.1 first when coming from an older version
- Code, pages, and docs say logo rather than series logo, since films draw their own

## Fixes
- The Profiles page loads again instead of failing on a backdrop setting that no longer exists
- Posters with a logo draw the logo selected for a film, season, or series instead of falling back to text

## Features
- Artwork Generator is Episode Poster Generator rebuilt, with the same settings and a much wider job
- The repository moved with the name; re-add it as jellyfin-plugin-artworkgenerator to keep getting updates
- Draws posters, thumbs, backdrops, and text logos, where before there were only episode posters
- Covers series, seasons, films, music videos, home videos, and anything else with a video
- Configuration is rebuilt in three parts, designs, logos, and profiles
- Profiles decide which items get which images and which design draws each one
- Every design renders portrait and landscape, so one design covers a tall poster and a wide thumb
- A design's two lines are now simply the title and the subtitle, whatever the item is
- Text position and alignment work on every design, not just the few that had them
- New Bloom design, pooling color from the frame behind the text
- New Grid canvas, tiling several extracted frames into one picture
- Logo designs build a text logo from any name field, with letter case, a line limit, and frame-filled letters
- Frame extraction is one set of server settings instead of a copy on every design
- Frames are ranked on tone, detail, contrast, and color rather than just clearing a threshold
- Optional setting drops a subtitle that only repeats the title
- A subtitle too long to fit can shorten to its code, shrink, or trim
- Two example designs per style, each showing a genuinely different look

## Fixes
- Seasons extract from their own episodes instead of falling back to the series backdrop
- Candidate images come from different episodes instead of clustering in one
- Heavily letterboxed frames scale back up to a usable size
- Portrait text is measured against both sides, so it no longer reads small
- Brush strokes stay thick on tall posters instead of piling into a cross
- Long titles trim at a word boundary rather than mid-word
- Descenders stay inside the safe area
- Borders, rules, and shadows scale with the poster
- A static graphic keeps its proportions
- An item with no name of its own says its one line in the larger type
- Generated images carry the item's metadata language

## Developer
- The generator, the settings model, and the configuration page are rebuilt around item kinds rather than episodes
- Built against the SkiaSharp 3.119.4 and Microsoft.Extensions 10.0.11 that Jellyfin 12.0 ships
- Designs are found by reflection, so adding one needs a class and an enum value
- Every label, option, and default is read from the settings models
- The shared generator is split into pipeline, text, and overlay
- Frame analysis is a single pass, under a megabyte per frame instead of three and a half
- Every one-time upgrade of an older configuration sits in its own file, to be deleted whole once installs have moved on
- Tests hold the documentation, the templates, and US spelling to the code

## Features
- Shadows, rules, and the Frame border now scale with the poster, so they read the same on a 4K frame as on a DVD rip instead of turning into a hairline or a slab
- Long titles that do not fit two lines fill the first line with whole words and trim only the second, at a word boundary, instead of cutting both lines mid-word

## Fixes
- Frame drew no border at all for an episode without a name, and ignored the Show Title setting
- Cutout no longer lets a two line title run into the bottom of the cutout letters
- Split center-crops the series poster into its panel instead of stretching artwork that is not 2:3
- Brush honours the Show Episode setting and keeps a wrapped title inside the area the strokes leave clear
- Timeline keeps the marker dot inside the safe area on the first and last episode
- Text blocks are reserved from the font's real ascent and descent, so descenders no longer hang past the safe area

## Developer
- Built against the SkiaSharp 3.119.4 and Microsoft.Extensions 10.0.11 packages Jellyfin 12.0 ships, since the plugin binds to the server's copies at runtime
- Text drawing moved from the removed SKPaint text members to SKFont, wrapped in a shared TextStyle so every style measures and draws with the same objects
- Standard and Split share one text stack; Numeral, Cutout, Brush, and Frame no longer hand-build their own paints
- Cutout renders through a canvas layer instead of a full-size scratch bitmap per poster; Split and Brush dispose their gradient shaders
- Letterbox detection scans the pixel buffer directly instead of a native call per pixel
- Bitmap scaling uses explicit cubic resampling now that FilterQuality is gone

## Developer
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- The dashboard menu entry now shows a icon instead of the generic folder
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10, and label sync has the token scope it needs

## Features
- Generated posters now appear in the episodes Edit Images dialog, so you can pick the frame you want instead of refreshing until you get a good one
- Choose how many alternate posters to offer in Edit Images, from 1 to 10 (default 3)
- Brush style can outline its stroke, sharing the Cutout styles outline toggle
- Element Spacing setting controls the gap between stacked poster elements, so every style spaces them the same way
- The font dropdown now lists the fonts actually installed on your server, and a font that is not installed is called out in the log instead of silently rendering in a substitute face
- Overlay colors collapse to an opacity control when Palette-Derived Colors is on, since the color itself comes from the image

## Breaking
- The scheduled task has been removed. Poster generation now runs entirely as a metadata provider - use a library metadata refresh, or pick a poster from Edit Images
- Processing history and its database have been removed, along with the Reset Processing History button. Jellyfins own refresh options now decide what gets regenerated

## Fixes
- Deleting an episode poster no longer left it permanently blank; there is no tracking state left to say the episode was already done
- Changing a custom font now takes effect; it used to be left out of the change detection entirely
- A tall logo no longer overlaps the episode code beneath it
- Long episode titles wrap to two lines again instead of being shortened to one
- Short titles no longer leave a gap between the episode code and the title
- Cancelling a refresh now stops frame extraction instead of letting it run to completion
- Generated posters are no longer written to the transcode directory and left behind
- Aspect ratios like 2.35:1 now parse correctly on servers with a comma decimal separator
- Saving the Posters tab no longer hangs on a spinner when the save fails, and no longer overwrites the settings on the other tab
- Settings added in a newer version no longer break saving for configurations written by an older one

## Developer
- The frosted panel shape and the brush stroke paths are disposed even when an exception unwinds
- Poster elements are positioned by a shared measure-then-place layout column instead of each style walking its own offsets, and titles are fitted to the height they are given as well as the width
- Poster configuration is never written back during plugin startup, so a failed config load can no longer overwrite good settings with defaults
- Poster rendering returns encoded bytes rather than temp files
- Removed the scheduled task, tracking database, configuration hashing, and around 900 lines of superseded code
- Shaders, mask filters, and image filters are disposed rather than left to finalization; HDR brightening no longer round-trips the whole bitmap through managed memory
- Example templates carry every current setting, and the bundled examples were regenerated
- Test suite grown from 21 to 39 cases, covering layout, title fitting, aspect ratio parsing, font resolution, and the generated image cache
- Bump Base to 2026.7.31

## Developer
- Bump Base to 2026.7.12

## Fixes
- Remove backdrops before using the current extracted frame as the new backdrop to prevent image bloat

## Fixes
- Frame seeking starts from a random phase each run, so refreshing an episode image picks a new frame instead of the same one

## Features
- Abbreviate tries the text before a divider, then the first sentence, then initials with periods

## Fixes
- Episode numbers and codes are pinned so title length cannot move them in any style
- Fade titles wrap to two vertical rows before long title handling engages

## Features
- New Long Titles dropdown with Ellipsis, Abbreviate, and Drop Name modes for titles that do not fit

## Fixes
- Cutout no longer overflows the poster edges on long episode titles. Every style now bounds long titles
- Safe area now applies the same pixel margin on all four sides based on poster height

## Polish
- Documentation and interface text cleanup

## Features
- New poster style - Striped - tilted pinstriped sash carrying the episode title
- New poster style - Frosted Glass - blurred glass panel behind the episode text
- New poster style - Fade - one-sided gradient with a large episode number and vertical title
- New poster style - Timeline - progress bar showing the episodes position within the season
- Palette-derived colors - overlay colors can be sampled from the episode frame
- Concurrent poster generation with a configurable worker count

## Performance
- Frame extraction now seeks with a stratified sequence instead of random retries
- Tracking database uses WAL mode, pooled connections, and a batched filter pass
- Poster settings hashes are cached instead of recomputed per episode
- JPEG encoding quality tuned from 100 to 92 for much smaller files

## Polish
- Brush strokes are feathered instead of hard-clipped for a painted look
- Cutout title shadow now uses the same soft blur as other styles
- Standard and Split separator lines follow the episode font color
- Fixed poster files not being truncated when re-rendered smaller
- All templates updated to the 10.11.24 settings format

## Developer
- Bump to base 2026.6.23
- File cleanup
- Update template files for import
- README cleanup
- Move demo creation to its own project folder
- Add tests just to keep me from going crazy
- Move poster descriptions to their CS file instead of maintaining in JS
- Move preview to button instead od rendering everytime

## Developer
- Migrate to shared web components
- Bump to base 2026.6.20

## Features
- Allow using the extracted image as a backdrop
- Allow using the series backdrop instead of needing to be extracted or nothing

## Fixes
- JS changes to ensure that buttons actually hide when unusable
- CSS changes to make this easier to maintain & less janky

## Features
- Live poster preview in the config page

## Developer
- New version numbering: 
- README updates
- Build updates for example images

## Fixes
- Attempt 4) to fix the plugin image

## Fixes
- Attempt 3) to fix the plugin image

## Fixes
- Attempt 2) to fix the plugin image

## Fixes
- Build fixes for 10.11.18

## Features
- Fix the Brush Poster Type from looking just truly terrible

## Chores
- Cleanup documentation and add build logic

## Fix
- Missing poster image
- Remove invalid image embedding

## Improvements
- Rename FFmpegService to FrameExtractionService and relocate to Canvas services directory
- Remove dead BrightnessService dependency from frame extraction service
- Strip BrightnessService to single responsibility (brightness adjustment only), remove unused analysis methods
- Remove unused public service properties from Plugin (CanvasService, CroppingService, FrameExtractionService, TrackingDatabase, TemplateExportService, LoggerFactory)
- Clean up JS, CSS, and HTML configuration pages (remove unused code, consolidate CSS variables, use Jellyfin built-in styles)

- Use Jellyfins built-in IMediaEncoder for frame extraction and tone mapping
- Remove custom FFmpeg tone mapping pipeline (ToneMapFilterService, HardwareFFmpegService, SoftwareFFmpegService, HardwareValidationService)

## Developer
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10
Fix 3.2 build issues.

## Developer
- Server routes moved under the Allow system access toggle, so a page needs one permission instead of two
- Shortened the configuration page help text

## Features
- Allow local resource calls, so a page can define named server side routes and call them with serverFetch while the server forwards each to its configured target
- Optional per page Allow system access toggle that runs a page without the sandbox, so its scripts can call the Jellyfin API and reach other resources on this origin
- Pages on a signed in tier can now be restricted to named users, defaulting to all users at that tier

## Developer
- Defining a route also runs its page unsandboxed, since the helper cannot reach the route from an opaque origin
- A route credential stored before encryption existed is upgraded on the next save rather than left in the clear
- Route credentials are encrypted at rest and never sent to a browser, and the configuration page posts back a sentinel so an untouched field keeps the stored value
- Forwarded requests carry the caller's headers minus a deny list, so the viewer's Jellyfin session is never handed to a route target
- Route targets must be absolute http or https URLs fixed in configuration, so a page cannot turn a route into an open proxy
- A restricted page is refused before its body is rendered, so content never reaches a viewer the list does not name
- An allow list is refused on an anonymous page at save time, and fails closed at serve time if the stored list is unusable
- Pages stay sandboxed by default, and an unsandboxed page still reaches the browser HTML encoded inside the wrapper's srcdoc
- Bump base to 2026.07.31

## Developer
- Serve every page under one Content-Security-Policy so a page behaves the same at any visibility tier
- Allow pages to load external resources and submit forms, which the anonymous tier previously blocked
- Allow pages to be embedded by the Jellyfin origin (frame-ancestors 'self')
- Serve page HTML as UTF-8 so single-file documents without a charset meta tag render correctly
- Sign in correctly when the web client is signed in to more than one server
- Reject unknown visibility tiers and malformed asset content types when configuration is saved
- Key the decoded asset cache to the asset itself, closing a stale-bytes window around a save
- Keep unsaved page edits when switching pages in the dashboard
- Declare targetAbi 10.11.10.0 to match the Jellyfin packages the plugin is compiled against

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.07.31
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- The dashboard menu entry now shows a dns icon instead of the generic folder
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10, and label sync has the token scope it needs

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.07.31

## Fixed
- The plain-http warning no longer logs the request URL's authority, which carried the update secret into the server log for providers whose credential lives in the URL's userinfo (ClouDNS DynURL, Directnic gateway URL). The warning now names the record's hostname instead
- A Data Protection key store that fails for an unexpected reason surfaces instead of being silently downgraded to plaintext credential storage; the expected failures (bad path, no permission, no service) still fall back as before

## Developer
- Address the outstanding CodeQL findings across the plugin and test projects (LINQ filtering and projection, ternary assignment, dictionary lookup, response disposal in the HTTP test stub)

## Fixed
- Resolve the TTL "1 = automatic" sentinel to a per-provider default instead of sending a literal one-second TTL (Gandi, GoDaddy, Spaceship, Hetzner, DNSExit)
- Yandex matches records by type as well as name, so an IPv4 update can no longer overwrite an AAAA or TXT record, and A/AAAA now update independently
- Spaceship writes the new record before removing stale ones, so a failed update leaves the old address serving instead of deleting the record
- Hetzner treats an accepted, still-applying action as success instead of timing out and counting a false failure toward backoff
- DNS Made Easy treats "no update required" as success instead of walking a healthy record into backoff
- DDNS.fm validates the response body instead of treating any HTTP 200 as success
- NS1 record creation sends the required zone, domain, and type fields, so first-time setup works
- Apex hostnames infer the correct domain when no zone is set (Porkbun, Dynadot, Spaceship, Dinahosting), and Dinahosting gained an optional Zone field
- OVH DynHost, DynDNS v1, DSLReports, and NearlyFreeSpeech.NET declare IPv4-only, so an IPv6 address is no longer recorded as pushed and endlessly re-pushed
- A record with one working address family is no longer paused by backoff when only the other family fails

## Developer
- Harden the publish workflow (release body via env, tag-derived version, fail-fast asset downloads, required tag on manual dispatch)
- Slash-command dispatch uses the JF_BOT_TOKEN secret instead of a placeholder
- CI packages with build.sh and verifies the zip contents, and build.sh parses build.yaml colon- and space-safely
- Response-parsing tests for every provider plus orchestrator and API tests

## Developer
- Bump Base to 2026.7.12
- Use ActivityLogger from Base 2026.7.12
- Use BackoffPolicy from Base 2026.7.12

## Feature
- Output logging to Activity Logs for better visibility

## Security
- Encrypt credentials saved through the generic plugin configuration endpoint instead of waiting for the next run
- Warn in the log when a record updates over plain http
- Show a dashboard warning when credential encryption is unavailable and secrets are stored in plaintext

## Developer
- Share one SecretProtector between the dashboard and generic save paths
- Snapshot the configuration per update run instead of mutating live records

## Fixes
- Prune record status against fresh record ids so a record added mid-run is not dropped

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.6.23
- Fix encryption of tokens to ensure they will not break between versions
- Migrate everything so it lives in the provider for ease of maintenance
- Reorganize files

## Documentation
- Creates Provider documentation per ddclient

## Fixes
- Check the DNS for current IP instead of always resending
- If the current DNS is internal, use the previous IP sent (previous behavior)

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.6.19
- Fix encryption of tokens to ensure they will not break between versions

## Fixes
- Remove URL from logging

## Initial release

This plugin acts as a DDNS resolver using Jellyfin as its host. A lot of this work will look very similar to [ddclient](https://github.com/ddclient/ddclient) which was a huge help and inspiration for this plugin. This takes the work they've taken and wraps it into a Jellyfin plugin for server owners don't want to manage more than one application.

versions.changelog:
# 🎬 Media Bar Arrives on Jellyfin 12

Media Bar **3.0.0.0** brings support for **Jellyfin 12**, including compatibility with both the classic desktop experience and Jellyfin's newer modern web layout.

> ## 🙌 Huge thanks to MakD and the upstream contributors
>
> Media Bar itself is the work of **MakD and the contributors to the upstream Media Bar project**. The plugin I maintain is primarily a Jellyfin wrapper around that work, exposing configuration and integration points so it can be installed and managed cleanly as a Jellyfin plugin.
>
> A huge amount of effort has gone into keeping Media Bar working across Jellyfin's changing web interface, especially for Jellyfin 12. The features, UI work and frontend improvements in this release are built on that upstream work, and the credit for that belongs to **MakD and everyone contributing there**.
>
> My part is largely packaging, integrating and exposing that work through Jellyfin's plugin system.

## ✨ New Features

* Added support for **Jellyfin 12**.
* Added support for Jellyfin 12's **modern React/MUI home screen layout**, alongside the existing classic desktop layout.
* Updated the bundled Media Bar frontend to the latest Jellyfin 12-compatible upstream version.
* Added Jellyfin 12-specific styling so Media Bar integrates correctly with the new web-client shell while retaining the existing appearance on the classic layout.
* Media Bar continues to ship its frontend assets directly with the plugin, ensuring the version displayed in Jellyfin matches the plugin version you've installed.

## 🛠️ Improvements

* Synced Media Bar with the latest Jellyfin 12-compatible upstream work.
* Improved Media Bar placement within the Jellyfin 12 home screen across both supported layouts.
* Improved layout behaviour on taller displays, ensuring Jellyfin's home-screen rows remain below the Media Bar content rather than overlapping its controls.
* Improved localisation handling when loading Jellyfin's translation chunks.
* Retained support for the **Get updates early** option for users who explicitly want to track unreleased upstream Media Bar changes.

## 🪲 Bug Fixes

* Fixed Media Bar being inserted in the wrong position when using Jellyfin 12's modern layout (#181).
* Fixed translated Media Bar strings falling back to English or producing JSON decoding errors for some languages (#185).
* Fixed home-screen rows overlapping Media Bar buttons on taller viewports.
* Fixed Jellyfin 12 layout differences that could cause Media Bar to render incorrectly compared with Jellyfin 10.11.

## ⚠️ Compatibility

* **Media Bar 3.0.0.0 supports Jellyfin 10.11.11 and Jellyfin 12.**
* Users on older Jellyfin 10.x versions should remain on a compatible **2.x** Media Bar release.
* Jellyfin 12 support includes both the **classic Desktop layout** and the newer **modern React/MUI layout**.
* A compatible **File Transformation 3.x** release is required.
* If you're using the **Get updates early** option, unreleased upstream Media Bar changes may behave differently from the frontend bundled and tested with this plugin release.

## Contributors

* austinnorgaard
* judarange

## ❤️ Support

If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27).

Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.
